text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President of right-wing disy party, Yiannakis Matsis, resigns but has been asked to remain at his post until party elections in June.
- Police discovered video tapes showing the delivery of army material in the possession of a Turk held on suspicion of spying.
- Matsis resigns. Bitter internal row comes to a sudden head. His move highlights the rift in the party.
- Britain is hopeful on prospect of direct talks between Greek and Turkish Cypriots. Sides are "coming to grips" with the situation, says British envoy Sir David Hannay.
- Is Disy heading towards a split? Matsis is under pressure to return to the party.
- Communist Akel seeks clarifications on the proximity talks which began this week to try to solve Cyprus's divisions.
- Alleged Turkish spies remanded on Sunday had video cassette of the delivery at a port of the T80U Russian tanks to Cyprus.
- Yiannakis Matsis' departure from Disy in June is final - the battle for the presidency in Disy begins.
